blogs.title: 13 Effective Email Segmentation Strategies, with Examples
blogs.author: Nikki Sequeira
blogs.content: Practical ways to personalize email with segmentation Generated by Klaviyo AI The article outlines 13 ways to segment email subscribers using engagement, shopping behavior, customer value, location, and preferences. Brand examples show how these segments inform welcome messages, offers, and follow-ups, while dynamic segmentation and AI help automate targeting. Engagement targeting: Focusing regular campaigns on engaged subscribers helps maintain list health and email deliverability. Customer journey: Acquisition source, browsing history, and past purchases help tailor welcome emails, product suggestions, and replenishment reminders. Value-based offers: Cart value, purchase amounts, lifetime value, and loyalty status can guide discounts and exclusive rewards. Support-aware messaging: Reviews and support interactions inform follow-ups, while customers with open support tickets can be excluded from marketing campaigns. Automated personalization: Dynamic segmentation updates groups as shoppers interact with a brand, while AI can help create segments and predict individual product interests or reorder timing. Sign up Get a demo Show AI generated summary Email segmentation is how you send fewer, more targeted messages to your subscribers. By splitting shoppers up into segments based on what you know about them, like their browsing behavior, preferences, purchases, spend, and more, you can increase revenue and improve brand reputation just by sending relevant messages. With dynamic segmentation, all of this happens automatically. When all your customer data is centralized in one CRM like Klaviyo, dynamic segmentation happens automatically as shoppers interact with your brand and fit different criteria. That might mean: Behavioral segmentation: Behavioral segmentation groups subscribers based on their interactions with all your channels. This enables you to tailor messaging based on what your subscribers actually do (e.g., engaging with your marketing, shopping in certain product categories, spending a lot or a little, or contacting customer support). Psychographic segmentation: Psychographic segmentation groups subscribers based on their interests, values, lifestyles, and personalities. This enables you to tailor your emails based on what people care about, not just the actions they’ve taken (e.g., sending emails about eco-friendly products to environmentally conscious subscribers). Demographic segmentation: Demographic segmentation groups subscribers by traits like age and location. This enables you to tailor emails to resonate with specific demographics (e.g., sending shoppers within a certain radius of your store an invitation to an upcoming local event). And with AI segmentation now available (more on this toward the end), you can consider the email segmentation ideas in this article as jumping off points for prompts that can create more complex segments and more relevant messages. 1. Email segmentation based on marketing engagement Targeting subscribers based on their engagement with your marketing is essential for maintaining the health of your email list. Consider engagement-based segmentation as non-optional, so your email deliverability stays high and you’re only reaching shoppers who want to hear from you. When Huda Beauty saw a YoY decline in overall performance, they decided to overhaul their content strategy, clean up their email list, and focus on targeting their most engaged subscribers. They now only send regular campaigns to subscribers who have engaged within the last 120 days, reserving full-list email blasts for major annual sales only. The results: 2x YoY growth in Klaviyo-attributed revenue . “With simple Klaviyo segmentation, we were able to clean up a lot of the deliverability issues that we had previously,” explains Phuong Ngo, CRM and loyalty manager at Huda Beauty. “It was a small thing that created a really big lift.” After a while, you’ll be able to use your subscribers’ engagement history to send messages on the channels they’re most likely to engage with. Provided you’re also building your text message, WhatsApp , and mobile app marketing lists, you can use AI-powered channel affinity to build segments based on channel engagement and automatically route campaigns to the channel subscribers are most likely to engage with next. 2. Email segmentation based on acquisition source How your new subscribers sign up for your email list—on your website, through a referral, via social media , in-store, etc.—tells you something about what they might want next from your brand. And that makes acquisition source a particularly helpful characteristic for segmenting your welcome series . In flows, you can accomplish segmentation with conditional splits and branching. Try tailoring your first messages to new subscribers based on their probable motivations: If they signed up from a promotional offer page, they may be interested in discounts. If they signed up for a newsletter before buying, they may be more interested in educational or brand content. If they signed up through a referral, they may already trust your brand because someone they know does. So try to entice them to make their first purchase. If they signed up when making a purchase, they may be enticed to come back for more. Try offering an incentive to leave a review or make a future purchase. Apparel brand Marine Layer , for example, has one welcome series for in-store subscribers and another for online subscribers. Those who visit a Marine Layer store in person are introduced to the brand’s website. For those who subscribe directly on their website, Marine Layer offers a coupon code for 10% off, and encourages them to locate their closest store . Marine Layer 3. Email segmentation based on recent sign-ups New subscribers may not be ready to buy, but they’ve indicated interest in your brand. Affirm their decision to subscribe by sharing top product features, brand storytelling, testimonials, and customer reviews. In addition to your welcome flow, those first few email campaigns are also great for gathering more data about your subscribers. For example, while new email subscribers may not be ready to download your app and receive push notifications , you may want to present them with the option to subscribe to text messages instead. Or, send a quiz to find out which products might be right for them. This email from furniture maker Keeps gives new subscribers a sampling of essential introduction content. They may want to click to get to know the mission, or they may be ready to skip forward to learn about the flagship products. Keeps also includes a customer review at the bottom of the email, which may be enough to prompt people to scroll back up and claim that free shipping code. Really Good Emails 4. Email segmentation based on browsing history Unlike when someone places an item in a cart, which signals high intent to buy, someone who views a product page on your website without adding an item to their cart is saying, “Hey, I’m just browsing. I’m not sure if I want to buy just yet.” That means you have some room to play with what you put in your emails for segments of shoppers who’ve only browsed certain product pages on your website. The goal is to strike a “relevance jackpot” with someone who needs a nudge toward check-out. One particularly helpful source of data for this type of segment is your self-service customer hub , where shoppers can manage their orders and returns, interact with customer service via web chat, and, most importantly, favorite or wishlist items they may want to purchase later. In this email segmentation example, scent brand Ashley & Co. sends a singular accessory offer for their clean buff cloth. It’s perfect for someone who may have been browsing their surface cleanse products, but wasn’t convinced enough to add one of those to cart. blogs.title: Klaviyo Customer Agent Use Cases That Cut Tickets & Lift Sales
blogs.author: Emil Gjorgjijev
blogs.content: How agencies build useful customer agent workflows Generated by Klaviyo AI Agency examples show how Klaviyo Customer Agent handles order questions, loyalty inquiries, class bookings, subscription changes, and damage claims. The post explains how live data, written rules, conversation reviews, and chat-triggered follow-ups connect customer service with marketing. Conversation-led improvements: Reviewing real chats helps teams prioritize unmet needs, fix incorrect answers, and test changes before release. Live data connections: Built-in capabilities and custom integrations let Customer Agent access order, loyalty, booking, and subscription data to answer questions and complete actions. Written operating rules: Brand guidance defines policies, required confirmations, and when sensitive or suspicious requests must go to a person. Service-informed marketing: Shared customer profiles support relevant follow-ups, recovery flows, and pauses on promotional messages while complaints remain open. Post-chat follow-ups: One agency reported 32% more follow-up flow revenue after using chat events to trigger product recaps, recommendations, and service check-ins. Sign up Get a demo Show AI generated summary Most teams plan an AI customer agent the way they plan a product catalog. They list what they sell, then try to cover it. I've found it works better to start with what customers actually say in their chats. As the ecommerce operations manager of ECD Digital Strategy , I lead AI automation for our DTC brands. Klaviyo Customer Agent is the AI customer agent that works from the same customer profile as your email, text messaging, web chat, and WhatsApp. That shared profile is what makes the powerful use cases below possible. The strongest Customer Agent builds share a few traits: Volume: Zac Fromson, cofounder of Lilo Social , describes a fragrance sample brand with thousands of monthly conversations where "most are repeat questions with known answers." Questions like that are the easiest to hand to an AI agent. A clock: Fromson points out that on a subscription brand, "most subscription questions are routine and come with a deadline." If nobody answers before the next charge, the order ships anyway. An AI agent that replies in seconds closes that gap, preventing the shipment from shipping if there are issues. Access to the systems where the answer lives: Roddy Smith, general manager North America of Andzen , an award-winning CRM lifecycle agency for DTC and ecommerce brands, built a connection to a studio's booking platform so the AI agent and the marketing team "share the same live view of each member." Once an AI agent can see and act on live data, a lot more of your conversation volume becomes resolvable. Written rules: Each build below spells out what the AI agent can say, what it can do, and when it hands the conversation to a person. That's what lets the team trust it with real customers. Here are 7 builds from agencies in the field, which cover use cases ranging from order tracking to class bookings to the follow-up emails that go out after a chat ends. 1. Start with the questions customers already ask Fromson's team works with a DTC fragrance sample brand that gets thousands of support conversations a month. About 36% of them need live order data to answer, such as: "Where is my order?" "It hasn't arrived." "How do I cancel?" How it works: live order data and late-order alerts Fromson and his team at Lilo Social use Customer Agent's out-of-the-box skills for looking up and changing orders, drawing on the brand's Klaviyo and Shopify data . In addition, they’ve built a custom Claude skill will connect the brand's warehouse system and add two things: A projected delivery date before a tracking number exists Flags for orders that are running late Late orders also trigger a Klaviyo flow message before the customer writes in. Fromson says this approach "cuts the number of tickets instead of only automating the replies." When Customer Agent cancels an order, it "confirms the cancellation in every downstream system before telling the customer it's done." When Customer Agent cancels the order, it confirms the cancellation in every downstream system before telling the customer it's done. Zac Fromson, Co-Founder Lilo Social 2. Put the brand's rules in writing For the same fragrance brand, Fromson says about 37% of inquiries are knowledge questions. Customers ask about sample authenticity, sizes, and shipping costs by market. Another 11% are loyalty questions about points balances, expiry, and redemption. Previously, Lilo Social reps opened Klaviyo daily to look up points and promo codes by hand. How it works: brand rules loaded into AI agent guidance Fromson and his team loaded the brand's rules around the following into the Customer Agent's guidance: Exact product size names Final-sale terms on samples No guaranteed shipping speeds Separate free-shipping thresholds for US and international orders A list of banned words This way, “Customer Agent never promises something the brand can't deliver," Fromson explains. A custom skill (which lets brands automate their unique use cases) lets it check balances, process redemptions, and explain why a promo code doesn't apply, all inside the conversation. 3. Let the conversations decide what you build For a welding and pipeline safety gear brand, my team at ECD stopped planning Customer Agent around the catalog and started planning it around the chats. How it works: a weekly review of every conversation Every Monday, an AI routine we built on Customer Agent APIs reads every conversation from the past week. It tags each one by topic, outcome, and buying intent. It flags where the AI agent got stuck, gave a wrong answer, or let a ready-to-buy shopper leave without a product link. Small fixes, like knowledge snippets and skill instructions, go live the same week. Before they do, we replay real shopper questions through the AI agent in preview mode, both before and after the change. Customer Agent drafts bigger builds, like new skills and follow-up flows, for our team to approve with a one-line email reply. The chats tell a different story than the catalog. Umbrella and shade questions were the biggest unmet need, with over 40% handed to the team. A gift loop we built from the catalog got zero mentions. The weekly loop also catches small gaps fast, like the AI agent saying a bundle didn't exist when 5 did. The results: higher scores on test conversations and nearly 3x conversion In the first 3 weekly cycles, 9 improvements went live, each tested on real shopper questions first. Here’s what we discovered: Up to 26 points better: Customer Agent's score on replayed shopper questions rose from 63% to 89% in a single cycle. Nearly 3x conversion where the conversations pointed us: Chats handled by the umbrella skill turned into orders at 19%, compared to 7% for chats overall. 67–78% resolved: That's the share of finished chats the AI agent resolves on its own, without the human team getting involved. 4. Book and cancel classes in-chat A boutique fitness studio runs every class, credit pack, and membership in their booking platform, Mariana Tek. Customer Agent couldn't reach it out of the box, and Klaviyo couldn't see it either. The team at Andzen built a custom middleware that connects the booking platform with Klaviyo, providing 3 years of data along with continued real-time updates on every member. How it works: booking, canceling, and live member data Signed-in members can see the live schedule, check their credits, review upcoming bookings, and book or cancel a class without leaving the chat. Behind the scenes, Andzen backfilled 3 years of history into Klaviyo. Now, 12 event types land within seconds: bookings, check-ins, cancellations, no-shows, orders, and membership changes. Credits, membership status, and attendance sit on every profile. The studio's rules live in Customer Agent's guidance, so every action follows them. For exam...

blogs.title: Redo Acquires Relist to Help Brands Sell More of What Comes Back
blogs.author: The Redo Team
blogs.content: Request a demo Take 10 minutes and see how Redo can help your business. Get started Or install on Shopify Redo today announced the acquisition of Relist, a platform that connects brands with the people reselling their products. Together, the two companies will give merchants a better option for returned inventory than selling it off at liquidation prices. Plenty of merchandise that comes back is still in excellent condition, and shoppers on secondhand marketplaces are already looking for it. Relist’s technology will first power Redo Managed Returns , sending excess and aging stock to the channels where it sells quickly and at the strongest price. A Note from Redo “We're building Redo to help brands get more value from every stage of commerce, including what happens after a return. Relist brings resale into that picture, giving merchants another way to turn returned inventory into revenue through the platform they already trust.” Sterling Snow, Co-Founder and CEO of Redo “Returns shouldn’t be a dead end.” Maneesh Karnati, Cofounder of Relist. Redo has acquired Relist. A Better Path for Returned Inventory Relist started by connecting brands to their resellers at the moment an item sells. Each time a seller completes a sale, the brand can reward them with store credit or a discount on their next purchase, which turns secondhand activity into a low-cost way to win repeat customers. Behind that sits a listing engine that lets shoppers upload a closet in minutes and post to several marketplaces at once. At Redo, that technology starts in the warehouse. Some items get refulfilled and others are consolidated and sent back to the merchant, but a meaningful share sits unsold or ends up as excess. Instead of defaulting that stock to liquidation, Relist will focus on two goals for merchants: Speed: moving items quickly after they come back. Value: getting the highest possible price for each one. It’s another step toward giving brands one partner across returns management and reverse logistics, rather than a patchwork of separate vendors. A Note from Relist “Returns shouldn’t be a dead end. Resale marketplaces have existed for decades, and billions of dollars in GMV move through them every year. Most returned items are in great shape, but brands have had no easy way to tap into that demand and get real value back. Joining Redo lets us plug resale directly into the returns flow, so every item finds its next customer at the best price and merchants recover revenue they used to write off.” Maneesh Karnati, Cofounder of Relist Looking Ahead Redo will continue investing in Relist’s technology and team, starting with Managed Returns and growing into wider capabilities for merchants and shoppers. Over the coming months, relist.co, the company’s social accounts, and its email list will move into a new Redo-owned experience that launches alongside these broader initiatives. We’re excited to welcome Maneesh and Ben, and grateful to the merchants and partners who trust us along the way. About Redo Market, sell, ship, and return on one platform. Redo is the all-in-one ecommerce platform for returns, payments, fulfillment, and AI-powered marketing. Upgrade the shopper experience at every interaction, and turn every order into the next one.
